samples.summary: New CLI hard-requires a `state` echo that older backends never send — version skew breaks `wafflebase login` against any deployed/self-hosted server that predates the backend half of this change
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` now rejects (400 "Invalid state") every callback whose `state` does not match the minted nonce (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206). The echo is produced only by the new `stateEcho` in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134. The CLI ships to users independently of the server (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:389 describe self-hosted backends), so a user on the new CLI + an unpatched backend gets a genuine callback with no `state`, sees "Invalid state" in the browser, and the CLI hangs until the 30s timeout with no diagnostic. There is no version negotiation or capability check anywhere in the login flow (login.ts:33-63). Fix belongs on the new CLI code (a clear error naming the server-version mismatch, or a documented minimum server version).

samples.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` discards non-envelope backend bodies, so Nest's default error responses (`{statusCode, message, error:"Not Found"}`) now lose their message on every converted call site
samples.evidence: `backendErrorEnvelope` keeps fields only when `data.error` is a plain object (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:100-107); otherwise it emits just the fallback `HTTP_ERROR` / `HTTP <status>`. The backend has no global exception filter — grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|APP_FILTER` over packages/backend/src returns nothing, and only docs-content.controller.ts:44 hand-builds `{error:{code,message}}` — so a 401/403/404 arrives as Nest's default `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document abc not found","error":"Not Found"}`. The passthroughs at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155, slides.ts:161 still enter their `if (body?.error)` branch (the string "Not Found" is truthy) but now print only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`, where they previously printed the server's `message` verbatim. Same loss in docs/import.ts:181,217,240, notes/import.ts:170,203,222, slides/import.ts:200,249,268, files/upload.ts:231, files/download.ts:66.

samples.summary: Emitters that still print bare text on stderr with a non-zero exit contradict the newly documented "every emitter builds the envelope" invariant
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1035-1039 now states that every emitter goes through `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`, naming the orchestrators, passthroughs and `schema`. But `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61` and :67 do `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` / `console.error(\`Workspace not found: ${query}\`)` followed by `process.exit(1)`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:74,90,108` do the same. An agent parsing stderr as one JSON line per failure — the contract this change strengthens — gets unparseable text from `ctx switch` and `login`.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill docs still show the old, unattributed envelope shape
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57 documents `{ "error": { "code": "CONFIRMATION_REQ", "message": ... } }` and packages/cli/skills/docs-read-content.md:86 documents the `TYPE_MISMATCH` body — both without the `command` field the CLI now always emits, and both pretty-formatted while the shipped output is one line. These files are what agents read to learn the contract (docs/design/cli.md §8), and they were not updated with the rest of the docs.

samples.summary: An over-long or non-string `nonce` is silently dropped, degrading the new binding to the old unbound behaviour with no signal to the client
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:31-40 passes `undefined` when `nonce` is absent, empty, non-string or longer than 128 chars; auth.controller.ts:127-131 then omits the `state` echo entirely. A client that sent a nonce and is waiting on the binding (any future or third-party CLI, and the current CLI if the nonce grows) gets a callback with no `state` and cannot distinguish "server does not support binding" from "server dropped my nonce" — it just fails or, worse, falls back to accepting unbound codes. A 400 on an invalid nonce would be observable; the silent drop is not.

finding.summary: New CLI hard-requires a `state` echo that older backends never send — version skew breaks `wafflebase login` against any deployed/self-hosted server that predates the backend half of this change
finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer` now rejects (400 "Invalid state") every callback whose `state` does not match the minted nonce (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206). The echo is produced only by the new `stateEcho` in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134. The CLI ships to users independently of the server (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:389 describe self-hosted backends), so a user on the new CLI + an unpatched backend gets a genuine callback with no `state`, sees "Invalid state" in the browser, and the CLI hangs until the 30s timeout with no diagnostic. verdict.reason: Verified as described. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206-210 unconditionally rejects any callback whose `state` does not equal the minted nonce, and nonceMatches (login.ts:164-169) returns false for a missing/null value, so a callback with no `state` at all is rejected with 400 "Invalid state". The `state` echo is produced only by the new backend code at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-135 (conditional on the new `state.nonce` stored via github-auth.guard.ts:26-37 and cli-auth.store.ts:13,30,38,60), so a backend predating this change redirects without `state`. The CLI is an independently published npm binary (packages/cli/package.json:2-15) that can target any server via --server/WAFFLEBASE_SERVER, defaulting to the hosted API (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:7,90-94), and self-hosted backends are a documented deployment (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42,121; packages/backend/README.md:389-391). No capability probe, fallback, or minimum-server-version check exists in the login flow (login.ts:17-63); the listener stays open by design (login.ts:203-210) and the flow dies at the 30s timeout with the misleading message "Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`." (login.ts:257-265). This is a new required field on a cross-package/cross-artifact contract that existing (older) counterpart servers do not supply — squarely in the blast-radius lane, and no refutation ground applies: the code is present, unguarded, and reachable. Minor correction to the finding's wording: the CLI does not hang indefinitely, it fails after 30s with an unrelated timeout message.

finding.evidence: `backendErrorEnvelope` keeps fields only when `data.error` is a plain object (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:100-107); otherwise it emits just the fallback `HTTP_ERROR` / `HTTP <status>`. The backend has no global exception filter — grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|APP_FILTER` over packages/backend/src returns nothing, and only docs-content.controller.ts:44 hand-builds `{error:{code,message}}` — so a 401/403/404 arrives as Nest's default `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document abc not found","error":"Not Found"}`. The passthroughs at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155, slides.ts:161 still enter their `if (body?.error)` branch (the string "Not Found" is truthy) but now print only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`, where they previously printed the server's `message` verbatim. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. formatter.ts:99-110 keeps upstream fields only when `data.error` is a non-array object; Nest's default body places `message` as a sibling of a STRING `error`, so `fields` is empty and both code and message collapse to the caller's HTTP_ERROR / "HTTP <status>" fallback — the server's message is never read. Grep for ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|APP_FILTER|Catch( across packages/ returns zero matches, so nothing reshapes backend errors globally; only docs-content.controller.ts:42-47 hand-builds {error:{code,message}}, while images.controller.ts:95, documents.controller.ts:109, workspace-scope.guard.ts:28 and tabs.controller.ts:122 throw plain-string exceptions producing the default shape on reachable 401/403/404 paths. The consumers are as cited: docs.ts:196-208 and 266-274, notes.ts:147-156, slides.ts:153-157 all enter their `if (body?.error)` branch because the string "Not Found" is truthy, and files/download.ts:64-66 forwards res.data with no guard at all. Tests at output.test.ts:244-267 cover only a well-formed {error:{...}} body and a null body, never the Nest default shape. This is a behaviour change to an exported symbol whose consumers now silently drop the server's diagnostic message — in lane for blast-radius and major under the rubric. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing guards against it, and the impact is only visible by leaving the diff to read the backend and the unchanged call sites.

finding.summary: New CLI + older backend = `wafflebase login` can never complete (version skew across independently released packages)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206 now rejects any callback whose `state` does not equal the freshly minted nonce. The echo is produced only by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134, and the CLI ships independently to npm (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:52 publishes @wafflebase/cli on its own version). Any self-hosted or not-yet-upgraded backend (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md) redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with no `state`, so the browser gets a bare `400 Invalid state`, the listener never resolves, and login fails after the 30s timeout at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:257-265 with the misleading message "Login timed out". The backend side is deliberately backward compatible (nonce optional), but the CLI side is not forward/backward compatible in the other direction, and nothing detects or reports the skew. Fix belongs on the new CLI code: detect a state-less callback and emit a specific "server does not support this CLI version" error rather than hanging.

verdict.reason: All claimed code exists as described. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206 hard-rejects any callback whose `state` does not equal the freshly minted nonce, and deliberately keeps the listener open, so the only exit for a state-less callback is the 30s timeout at login.ts:257-265 with the misleading message "Login timed out". The `state` echo is produced solely by packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-134, and it is conditional on `state.nonce`, which is optional throughout the backend (cli-auth.store.ts:13,27-31; github-auth.guard.ts:34-39) — so any backend predating this change redirects with `code` but no `state`. The CLI ships independently to npm (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:52-59, versioned from packages/cli/package.json; the backend is not an npm artifact per the comment at lines 49-51), and the docs explicitly support pointing the CLI at arbitrary self-hosted servers (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:30,104), with the default at packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:7. That makes new-CLI/old-backend a real, documented, reachable configuration in which `wafflebase login` can never complete and reports no useful cause. This is in the blast-radius lane: a new required field on the callback contract that existing call sites (deployed backends in a separately released package) do not supply, with no detection or fallback anywhere in the CLI. No guard, version negotiation, or caller elsewhere makes it unreachable.
